scenes.headline: How OpenQodex makes a reviewer answer every hit
scenes.sub: Scanners on your changed lines, then a separate reviewer, then a script.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lint! This open source reviewer runs before you push, and makes a model answer for every scanner hit.

scenes.text: Scanners flag the changed lines. A separate, read-only reviewer must raise or drop every hit, and a script sends the answer back until it does.
scenes.say: Scanners flag your changed lines. A separate reviewer must raise or drop every hit, and a script sends the answer back until it does.

steps.say: Your unpushed work is copied into a frozen snapshot. Everything after this reads the copy.
A scanner runs only if the change holds a file it reads. Hits are cut to the changed lines.
A separate Claude Code or Codex process gets the brief. It can read the snapshot, and nothing else.
A script checks its answer and sends back what is wrong, at most twice. Then, a verdict.

items.say: Every candidate gets exactly one answer: raised, or dropped with a reason and a line.
Findings start on a line the change touched.
The prose is short and never names the scanner.
And every changed line was in front of the reviewer.

steps.say: On the demo, twenty-six candidates went in, and ten findings came out.

steps.note: found with no scanner behind it
steps.say: A pagination bug had no scanner behind it. The reviewer found it.

scenes.label: built-in scanners, where the launch slide says 100+
scenes.note: 1,089 semgrep rules, if you count rules instead
scenes.say: One correction. The launch says a hundred plus scanners. The code has thirteen.

left.title: As installed
items: The gate only looks up a review
left.say: Before a push, nothing reviews. The gate looks for a finished review, and by default only warns.

right.title: With a threshold set
items: No review on record: push denied
An incomplete review still never blocks
right.say: Set a threshold, and a missing or failing review stops the push.

scenes.text: A forced answer per hit makes silence impossible. It does not make the answer right, so set a threshold.

recap: Scanners only on the lines you changed
One checked answer for every hit
Thirteen scanners; the gate warns by default
scenes.say: Scanners on your changed lines, a reviewer that answers every hit, and a gate you should turn up.
